answer: AI-agent economies blunt Sybil attacks by pricing identity as a stake, not a signup. Each new persona must post collateral slashed on provable misbehavior, and unlock a cipher-bound signing handle that costs real resources to mint. Splitting one attacker into many wallets multiplies frozen capital instead of diluting it: the same harm needs many bonded positions, each forfeitable. Reputation acts like a prism, scattering one actor across correlated copies sharing exposure, so a fresh velvet-smooth account earns nothing until it does real work. Cost scales linearly; reward does not.
